body:
The academic evidence broadly supports the legends' ideas:
- Cheap stocks (value) and profitable, high-quality stocks have historically earned premiums.
- Profitability and value are negatively correlated, so combining them works better than either alone. This is "quality at a reasonable price," which is what Buffett/Munger and QGLP practise.
- Buffett's own record is largely explained by leveraged exposure to cheap, safe, quality stocks.
title: fundamental_frameworks › Takeaway

body:
- **Annual-report reading checklist (synthesis):**
  1. *Auditor's report & CARO annexure* – qualifications, emphasis of matter, going-concern, KAMs; CARO comments on loans to related parties, defaults, fraud reporting. *Auditor change mid-term* = top red flag (Manpasand, Vakrangee above).
  2. *Related party transactions (AS/Ind AS 24 note + AOC-2)* – purchases/sales with promoter entities, loans/advances/guarantees to group cos, royalty to promoter entities; cross-check against subsidiaries' and private promoter cos' disclosures (Kaynes, Gensol, Brightcom).
  3. *Contingent liabilities & guarantees* vs net worth (corporate guarantees to group cos).
  4. *Cash flow vs profit* – cumulative 5–10 yr CFO/PAT well below ~0.7–0.8, or FCF persistently negative while reporting profit growth.
  5. *Working capital* – receivable days and inventory days rising faster than sales; "loans and advances" / "other current assets" ballooning.
  6. *CWIP and capitalised expenses* – CWIP stuck for years; R&D/"technical know-how"/interest capitalised (Kaynes ₹180 cr capitalised).
  7. *Other income* as share of PBT; interest income on funds that look idle while company borrows (cash + debt both high = classic Indian red flag).
  8. *Subsidiaries / step-downs / overseas entities* – many small subsidiaries, write-offs, impairments delayed (Brightcom).
  9. *Promoter remuneration* vs PAT and vs peers; commission structures.
  10. *Shareholding* – promoter pledge trend, promoter selling, preferential allotments/warrants to unknown entities, frequent fund-raises (Brightcom preferential issue).
- **Background on older blow-ups [BACKGROUND, not re-verified this session]:** Satyam (Jan 2009) – Ramalinga Raju confessed to ~₹7,000 cr inflation incl. fictitious cash balances; lesson: verify cash vs interest income; PwC later penalised. IL&FS (2018) – AAA-rated group defaulted with ~₹90,000+ cr debt; 300+ subsidiaries; rating agencies penalised; lesson: complex group structure, rating complacency. DHFL (2019) – Cobrapost alleged ~₹31,000 cr diverted via shell companies; later the first NBFC/HFC resolved via IBC (Piramal); lesson: loans to related "builder" entities, ALM mismatch. Yes Bank (2020) – RBI moratorium March 2020, under-reported NPA divergence flagged by RBI in prior years, SBI-led rescue, AT1 bonds written off; founder Rana Kapoor arrested; lesson: NPA divergence disclosures in annual report, rapid corporate-loan growth to stressed groups. Gitanjali Gems (2018) – Mehul Choksi linked to the ~₹13,000+ cr PNB LoU fraud with Nirav Modi; lesson: high receivables/inventory in jewellery, promoter pledging. Each of these should be verified with primary sources before citation.
- **Scoring tools:** Beneish M-score (8 variables; > −1.78 commonly treated as likely manipulator), Altman Z-score (distress; original manufacturing cut-offs 1.81/2.99; EM-variant Z'' for emerging markets), Piotroski F-score (0–9, 8–9 strong). Trendlyne/Screener users often build these manually. [BACKGROUND – thresholds standard in literature; no Indian-specific validation fetched.]
- Pattern across cases: auditor resignation + preferential issues/QIPs + aggressive promoter communication + retail/finfluencer hype + rising pledge → highest-risk combination.
title: india_toolkit_redflags › Inferences

body:
- Suggested process for the playbook: Screen → forensic overlay (CFO/PAT, receivable days, pledge, auditor tenure/changes, RPT % of revenue, other income % of PBT) → read 3–5 years of annual reports + last 8 concalls (check guidance vs delivery) → rating rationales → shareholding (promoter, MF/FII trends, bulk deals) → Valuepickr thread for scuttlebutt → valuation (PEG, EV/EBITDA vs history) → sizing with a "kill list" of red flags (auditor resignation, rating non-cooperation, rising pledge, preferential issues to obscure entities, finfluencer/Telegram promotion, SME listing with sharp post-listing run-up).
- Books referenced by Indian investors [BACKGROUND]: *Coffee Can Investing* (Mukherjea, Bajaj, Rao), *The Unusual Billionaires* (Mukherjea), *Diamonds in the Dust* (Mukherjea et al.), *100 Baggers* (Mayer).

body:
- **Interim order (3 Jul 2025):** SEBI barred JS Group entities from dealing in securities. It impounded ₹4,843 crore, the largest impounding order SEBI has ever made, calling it "prima facie unlawful gains". The order runs to 105 pages. — [Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/amp/markets/news/sebi-bars-jane-street-orders-rs-4844-cr-disgorgement-market-manipulation-125070400081_1.html); [SCC Online](https://www.scconline.com/blog/post/2025/07/09/sebi-restrains-jane-street-group-from-accessing-securities-market/)
- **Profit breakdown, Jan 2023 to Mar 2025:**
  - Index and stock options gains were about ₹43,289 crore.
  - Losses were ₹7,208 crore in stock futures, ₹191 crore in index futures and ₹288 crore in cash.
  - That nets to ₹36,502 crore. Bank Nifty options alone contributed ₹17,319 crore.
  - One outlet instead reports ₹36,671 crore net, with ₹44,358 crore from index options.
  - Sources: [Wright Research](https://www.wrightresearch.in/blog/why-did-sebi-ban-jane-street-from-indian-markets/); [Republic World](https://www.republicworld.com/business/sebi-banned-jane-street-after-rs-36500-cr-windfall-in-india-heres-what-you-need-to-know); [Angel One](https://www.angelone.in/news/jane-street-entities-made-over-rs-36000-crore-in-derivatives-trading-sebi)
- **Alleged mechanics, part 1 (intraday "pump then dump"):**
  - In the morning, JS bought large amounts of Bank Nifty constituent stocks and futures, lifting the index.
  - At the same time it built bigger short options exposure, such as selling calls or buying puts.
  - Later in the day it sold the cash and futures positions. The index fell and the options book profited.
  - Source: [Mondaq / Mansukhlal Hiralal](https://www.mondaq.com/india/securities/1648508/sebi-update-%7c-interim-order-against-jane-street-group-for-alleged-index-manipulation); [Legal500](https://www.legal500.com/developments/thought-leadership/sebi-update-interim-order-against-jane-street-group-for-alleged-index-manipulation/)
- **Alleged mechanics, part 2 ("Extended Marking the Close"):** JS traded aggressively in the final hour of expiry days to move the settlement level, for example on 10 Jul 2024. SEBI says JS also used this in Nifty on days in May 2025, after NSE's Feb 2025 caution letter. — [Wright Research](https://www.wrightresearch.in/blog/why-did-sebi-ban-jane-street-from-indian-markets/); [Business Today](https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/story/sebi-cracks-down-on-jane-street-in-landmark-derivatives-market-case-484348-2025-07-11)
- **Scope of the order:** It covers 18 Bank Nifty days and 3 Nifty expiry days. SEBI said the order "is not a show-cause notice" and that its probe extends to the Nifty 50, Sensex and other indices. — [Republic World](https://www.republicworld.com/business/sebi-clarifies-jane-street-interim-order-is-not-show-cause-probe-expands)
- **Jane Street's response:** It "disputes the findings" of the order. — [Angel One](https://www.angelone.in/news/jane-street-entities-made-over-rs-36000-crore-in-derivatives-trading-sebi)
- **Ban lifted:** Trading resumed after the ₹4,843.5 crore deposit into escrow. SEBI told exchanges to monitor JS trades and positions closely until proceedings end. — [Business Today, 19 Jan 2026](https://www.businesstoday.in/amp/markets/stocks/story/jane-streets-india-arm-saw-six-fold-surge-in-trading-gains-before-sebi-clampdown-report-511483-2026-01-19)
- **JSI Investment Pvt (India arm), year to Mar 2025, per Bloomberg citing filings:**
  - Net trading gains were ₹4,700 crore (~$517m), against ₹790 crore the year before, about six times higher.
  - After-tax profit was ₹2,840 crore, up 494%.
  - Source: [Business Today](https://www.businesstoday.in/amp/markets/stocks/story/jane-streets-india-arm-saw-six-fold-surge-in-trading-gains-before-sebi-clampdown-report-511483-2026-01-19)
- **India revenue:** Jane Street netted about $2.3bn from Indian equity options trading in 2024, per Bloomberg. I could see only the headline; the article returned 403. — [Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/amp/markets/news/jane-street-nets-2-3-bn-from-booming-india-equity-options-trading-125052301072_1.html)
- **SAT appeal (Sep 2025):** Jane Street appealed to SAT, alleging SEBI bias and withheld documents. These included the Integrated Surveillance Department report and SEBI–NSE correspondence. — [Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/markets/news/jane-street-files-appeal-in-sat-alleging-sebi-bias-in-probe-125090301189_1.html); [Outlook Business](https://www.outlookbusiness.com/news/market-probe-escalates-jane-street-moves-sat-for-full-disclosure-on-sebis-order-on-index-manipulation-allegation)
- **SEBI expanded the probe (Sep 2025),** citing inadequate data and ongoing complaints. — [Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/markets/news/sebi-expanded-probe-jane-street-market-manipulation-125091601192_1.html); [Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/markets/news/sebi-ramps-up-jane-street-probe-amid-inadequate-data-ongoing-complaints-125090500792_1.html)
- **SAT hearing (Oct 2026):**
  - SEBI said it had supplied more than 10 GB of data. It said JS should explain the "mode, manner and reasons" for its trades.
  - SEBI said the interim order could "probably be vacated" if JS satisfies it that the trades were not manipulative.
  - SEBI refused to hand over counterparty data.
  - JS argued that some Bank Nifty stock moves ran against its positions.
  - Sources: [Business Today, 6 Oct 2026](https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/story/sebi-tells-sat-that-jane-street-has-enough-data-to-respond-to-market-manipulation-charges-559953-2026-10-06); [Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/amp/markets/news/jane-street-should-explain-trading-strategies-sebi-tells-sat-in-hearing-126100601048_1.html); [Lapaas Voice](https://lapaasvoice.com/sebi-tells-sat-jane-streets-document-list-is-not-a-short-list-refuses-counterparty-data)
- **SAT reserved its order on 21 Oct 2026** on JS's plea for more documents. This is a procedural plea, not a ruling on the merits. — [LiveLaw](https://www.livelawbiz.com/securities-law/sat/securities-appellate-tribunal-reserves-order-jane-street-challenge-sebi-non-disclosure-relevant-documents-555493); [NewsBytes](https://www.newsbytesapp.com/news/business/sat-reserves-order-in-jane-street-document-disclosure-case/story)
- **Market impact:** F&O activity fell by almost 20% after the ban. — [Kotak Neo](https://www.kotakneo.com/investing-guide/futures-and-options/jane-street-sebi-ban-f-and-o-volumes-drop/)

`case_study:celsius-2020-2025` · tickers US-CELH · confidence: verified

Split-adjusted (3:1, Nov 2023): ~$1-1.5 in early 2020 [unverified] -> ~$99 (Mar-May 2024; YTD high $98.72 in May): ~60-70x. Driver: 'better-for-you' fitness energy drink sold to young women/gym users, then the Aug 2022 PepsiCo long-term US distribution deal (Pepsi invested ~$550m for ~8.5% [unverified]) that put Celsius in Pepsi's DSD network nationwide; revenue roughly tripled 2022-23 [unverified]. Mostly revenue/EPS growth, but P/E also peaked near 100x [unverified]. Reversal: Pepsi had over-ordered and then destocked — Q3 2024 revenue -31% to $266m, net income -92% — while retail scanner sales still grew ~7%; Alani Nu, Ghost and others took share; stock -73% (May-Sept 2024 to ~$32), -52% in 2024, low ~$21 early 2025 [unverified]. Feb 2025: bought Alani Nu for $1.8bn (cash + $500m stock), stock +~20-30%; closed Apr 1 2025. EARLY SIGNAL (up): distribution step-change into a national DSD system, measured in scanner data before reported revenue. EARLY SIGNAL (down): reported revenue running far ahead of scanner sell-through in 2023-24 — distributor inventory build. Who caught it: retail/momentum; no documented famous name. LESSON: a distribution deal gives a one-time step change; when sell-in (reported sales) outruns sell-through (scanner data), the destocking reversal is predictable — a direct echo of Monster's playbook but at a much higher price.

- **Start → end:** ~$1-1.5 split-adj (2020) [unverified] → ~$99 peak (2024); ~$21 low (2025) [unverified] (~60-70x up, -79% down)
- **EPS vs rerating:** revenue/EPS + P/E to ~100x
- **Max drawdown:** -73% (May-Sep 2024); ~-79% to early 2025
- **Early signal:** up: Pepsi DSD deal 2022; down: sell-in > scanner sell-through
- **Who caught it:** not documented
- **Ended/stalled:** May 2024 peak
- **Lesson:** distribution step change is one-time; monitor scanner vs reported sales
- **Sources:** [1](https://www.fool.com/investing/2025/01/12/why-celsius-stock-plunged-52-last-year) · [2](https://www.fool.com/investing/2024/11/06/why-celsius-stock-crashed-today) · [3](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2024-05-28/celsius-shares-celh-sink-most-in-three-years-on-sales-growth-concerns) · [4](https://www.bevnet.com/news/2025/celsius-acquires-alani-nu-for-1-8-billion) · [5](https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/celsius-holdings-completes-acquisition-alani-nur-2025-04-01)

body:
`case_study:garware-technical-fibres-2013-2024` · tickers: GARFIBRES · confidence: verified

Split-adjusted ₹10.2 (Jan 2013) → ATH ₹960 (Dec 2024) ≈94x; standalone P/E 4.9 → 42 (8.6x) × implied EPS ~10.9x. ₹737 on 19 Nov 2026 (−23%). Drawdowns were mild: −35% (2016), −34% (COVID), −38% (Dec 2024–Mar 2026). Early signal in filings: value-added products (aquaculture cage nets for salmon farms, sports nets, geosynthetics, specialty ropes) rose from ~35% of the mix in FY14 to ~75% in FY20 (~80% by 2026). Aquaculture is ~35% of revenue and the highest-margin segment. Consolidated sales grew only modestly (₹782 cr FY15 → ₹1,018 cr FY19), but OPM rose from 10% to 19% and PAT tripled (₹43 cr → ₹126 cr). Profit growing 3x faster than revenue at a 5x P/E is the classic mix-shift signature. Stalled: since FY21 revenue growth has been ~8–10%, P/E has stayed at 30–40, and the stock has gone sideways for about four years (₹636 end-2021 → ₹737). Lesson: mix shift gives a one-time margin step-up plus a rerating. After that the stock compounds only at revenue growth, so the rerating phase is where the multibagger is made.

Key data: **start_year**: 2013; **end_year**: 2024; **start_price**: 10.2; **end_price**: 960; **price_nov2026**: 737; **multiple**: ~94x; **pe_start**: 4.9; **pe_end**: 42.2; **eps_multiple_implied**: ~10.9x; **max_drawdown**: -35% in run; **early_signals**: VAP mix 35%→75%; PAT 3x on sales +30%; P/E ~5; **ended**: growth normalised ~10%; sideways since 2021; **lesson**: mix-shift step-up is a one-time engine

Sources: <https://www.screener.in/company/GARFIBRES/> · <https://trendlyne.com/posts/3096532/garware-technical-fibres-spreads-its-nets-far-and-wide> · <https://businesstoday.in/markets/stocks/story/garware-technical-fibres-ceo-sees-positive-q2-outlook-value-added-products-in-focus-548325-2026-08-10>

body:
**Hidden trap: DHFL's 33% AUM growth and low reported NPAs** (`case_study:hidden-trap-dhfl-growth`, verified). THE GOOD NUMBER: India's third-largest housing financier grew AUM ~33% to ~Rs 1.1 lakh cr in FY18 (Motilal Oswal), loan book Rs 91,932 cr (+28%), profit growth ~25%, low reported NPAs, valuation below HDFC. WHY IT LIED: the growth mix shifted to project/developer and other non-retail loans (project loans +55% YoY in Q3 FY18, non-retail +52% YoY), and much of it went to little-known entities later alleged to be linked to the Wadhawan promoters (Cobrapost: ~Rs 31,000 cr). The book was long-dated but funded with commercial paper and MF money. Low NPAs in a fast-growing book are mechanical: new loans have not had time to default. When IL&FS defaulted (Sep 2018) and DSP MF dumped DHFL paper, refinancing froze; default June 2019; equity wiped out in the 2021 Piramal resolution. TEST: for lenders read growth by segment, ALM buckets (1-year gap), CP share of liabilities, top-20 borrower exposure and related-party links; compare NPAs against loans seasoned 2-3 years (lagged NPA), not today's book. LESSON: in a lender, fast growth plus low NPAs is the ingredients list of a future problem unless funding is long and the book is granular retail.

**Hidden trap: Yes Bank's 17.7% ROE and 1.28% gross NPA** (`case_study:hidden-trap-yes-bank-roe`, verified). THE GOOD NUMBER: in FY18 Yes Bank reported ROE 17.7%, RoA 1.6% and gross NPA 1.28% (down from 1.72% the previous quarter) with loans up ~54%, numbers that rivalled HDFC Bank and earned a premium valuation; the stock peaked ~Rs 393-404 in Aug 2018. WHY IT LIED: ROE in a bank equals reported profit after provisions; under-provisioning lifts it. RBI's own inspections found NPA divergence of ~Rs 4,177 cr (FY16) and ~Rs 6,355 cr (FY17), i.e., reported NPAs were a fraction of real ones, and these divergences were publicly disclosed in 2017. A 54% loan growth rate in a corporate book is evergreening risk, and the lending was concentrated in groups that later failed (ADAG, Essel, DHFL, IL&FS, Cox & Kings, Jet). Low-cost deposits (CASA) were thin, so the bank paid up for bulk money. Sep 2018: RBI refused to extend the founder's term. GNPA went 1.3% (FY18) -> 7.4% (Sep 2019); moratorium Mar 2020; stock ~Rs 5.6. TEST: compare loan growth with system growth (3x system = red), read divergence notes, list top exposures by group, check CASA and cost of funds; ROA for a bank should be earned with granular retail, not by lending to stressed promoters. LESSON: a high ROE is a result, not a quality; in lenders the denominator of risk shows up 2-3 years later. Contrast HDFC Bank, whose ROE came with low-cost deposits and seasoned retail assets.

body:
**Date:** 2026-11-26 · **Analyst:** Claude · **Status:** live (not practice). Its paper calls are scored.
**Purpose:** test the deep-dive method on a company **drawn at random**. This is test material (L9, L21), so there is
**no buy/sell verdict**. Outputs: decision card v1.5 and dated probabilistic calls, scored later against naive base rates.
**Roadmap:** stage 2 (filters) → 3 (signals) → 4 (deep dive) → 5 (valuation) → 6 (decision) → 7 (scoreboard). New in this dive:
(a) consensus forward P/E beside our scenarios (L47); (b) news run plus L50 verification; (c) worksheet core-EPS inputs (L44).
It unlocks the first live test of a **post-merger entity**, which has no usable own history, and of **pharma-specific S2 checks**
(USFDA status, US price erosion, API/China dependence). This is research, not SEBI-registered advice.
